newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel income from foreign reserves falls.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel income from foreign reserves falls.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Thursday its income from foreign reserves dropped sharply in 1996 even though foreign reserves grew by $3.3 billion to $11.4 billion at the end of the year.
In dollar terms, income fell to $301 million from $847 million in 1995 after returns on reserves declined to 4.9 percent from 8.3 percent in 1995.

"The decline in dollar income, despite the rise in average reserves, was due to the strengthening of the dollar against other currencies, which resulted in a negative contribution because of exchange differential from non-dollar currencies," the central bank said.
The bank added that it posted capital losses from declining prices for U.S. bonds, which make up an important part of its portfolio.

In January, the Bank of Israel said it expected to post a 1996 loss of approximately 400 million shekels, its first since 1983, part of which it said was due to lower income from foreign currency reserves.
